reference_implementation.observed_title: Causal inference in the medical domain: a survey

paired_result.interpretation: Both implementations returned the same title/year result and the same response digest for this one DOI. The single-record runner summary is not an estimate of general accuracy or reliability.
paired_result.timing_interpretation: One wall-time observation per implementation; the 1.532s and 1.626s observations do not establish a stable latency or cost difference.

candidate: Accepts one to ten caller-selected unique bare DOI records with expected title/year.
Writes JSON to stdout only and does not modify repository files.
Uses a fixed HTTPS host, blocks redirects, caps response size and read duration, and reports explicit failures.
task103_runner: Normally processes the source registry, detects duplicate DOIs, computes aggregate metrics, and writes a JSONL source manifest.
Uses a 30-second socket timeout and up to four attempts per DOI; actual attempt count was not instrumented in this run.

related_registered_provider_evidence.scope: One other DOI had matching live Crossref/OpenAlex title/year fields plus a synthetic changed-year negative control; it does not establish broad provider quality or replacement.

limitations: One DOI and one invocation per implementation do not estimate correct-completion rate, broad applicability, availability, reliability, maintainability, or risk.
No external ground-truth source was used; matching provider responses are not proof of metadata correctness or source authenticity.
Retry count for the Task 103 runner was not instrumented, so its exact request count is unknown.
The two wall-time values are single observations and do not establish a stable latency, resource, or economic-cost advantage.
Raw provider response bytes were not retained; only their shared SHA-256 digest was recorded.

disposition.basis: The paired result confirms one matching outcome but is too narrow to establish replacement or retirement. The wrapper and Task 103 runner have different task and side-effect contracts; preserve uncertainty and the current optional default-off entry pending additional consumer-relevant same-task evidence.
